purpose: How can five different display frames keep the same Euler count?
meaning: A Platonic solid is a convex polyhedron with congruent regular polygon faces and the same number of faces meeting at each vertex. These five models have vertex count V, edge count E and face count F satisfying V−E+F=2. Choosing a new solid changes actual connections and counts; a projected edge crossing is not an extra vertex.

definition.setting: A model maker chooses a regular convex display frame. Count its corners, connecting edges and polygon faces while the actual edge skeleton changes.

signature.s: Discrete solid choice: 1 tetrahedron, 2 cube, 3 octahedron, 4 dodecahedron, 5 icosahedron

conditions: Use a whole selection from one through five. These are convex regular solids with unit-length edges and closed surfaces without holes; count actual spatial vertices, edges and faces rather than crossings in the fixed view.
definition.domain_notes: Choose exactly one of five regular convex solids: 1 tetrahedron, 2 cube, 3 octahedron, 4 dodecahedron, 5 icosahedron. The index is a selection label, not a physical quantity. Every modeled edge is one unit long. A fixed orthographic view shows all edges, including normally hidden edges. Screen crossings do not create new vertices. Face count and the Euler relation are topological counts, not volume or projected area.

grammar.formation_rule: A Platonic solid is a convex polyhedron with congruent regular polygon faces and the same number of faces meeting at each vertex. These five models have vertex count V, edge count E and face count F satisfying V−E+F=2. Choosing a new solid changes actual connections and counts; a projected edge crossing is not an extra vertex.
grammar.precedence: Each edge belongs to two faces, so face count times sides per face equals twice edge count. Each edge has two ends, so vertex count times edges per vertex also equals twice edge count. Explicit coordinate edge skeletons supply the same counts. Substituting those integer counts gives two for V−E+F in every displayed model. This verifies these five cases rather than proving a general topological theorem.
